headline: Kafka's session timeout is broker-side liveness detection.

quoteChecks.quote: `session.timeout.ms` — The timeout used to detect client failures when using Kafka's group management facility. The client sends periodic heartbeats to indicate its liveness to the broker

frags.frag: `session.timeout.ms` — The timeout used to detect client failures when using Kafka's group management facility. The client sends periodic heartbeats to indicate its liveness to the broker

_hay: quote (§session.timeout.ms, S118, kafka.apache.org/43/configuration/consumer-configs): "session.timeout.ms — The timeout used to detect client failures when using Kafka's group management facility. The client sends periodic heartbeats to indicate its liveness to the broker." "if no heartbeats are received by the broker before the expiration of this session timeout, then the broker will remove this client from the group and initiate a rebalance."

headline: Cadence is explicitly bounded by the session window.

quoteChecks.quote: `heartbeat.interval.ms` — The expected time between heartbeats to the consumer coordinator

frags.frag: `heartbeat.interval.ms` — The expected time between heartbeats to the consumer coordinator

quoteChecks.quote: typically should be set no higher than 1/3

frags.frag: typically should be set no higher than 1/3

_hay: quote (§heartbeat.interval.ms, S118): "heartbeat.interval.ms — The expected time between heartbeats to the consumer coordinator when using Kafka's group management facilities. Heartbeats are used to ensure that the consumer's session stays active..." Default: 3000 (3 seconds); must be set lower than session.timeout.ms, typically no higher than 1/3 of that value. group.consumer.session.timeout.ms default: 45000 (45 seconds).

headline: Reclaim is group-level, not per-message.

quoteChecks.quote: the broker will remove this client from the group and initiate a rebalance

frags.frag: the broker will remove this client from the group and initiate a rebalance

_hay: quote (S118, session.timeout.ms continuation): "the broker will remove this client from the group and initiate a rebalance" — partition assignments are reclaimed by group membership, not by per-message lease; a dead consumer's partitions re-assign to survivors.

headline: Kubernetes probes are platform-polled, not worker-pushed.

quoteChecks.quote: Kubernetes provides liveness probes to detect and remedy

frags.frag: Kubernetes provides liveness probes to detect and remedy

quoteChecks.quote: cannot recover except by being restarted

frags.frag: cannot recover except by being restarted

_hay: quote (S119, kubernetes.io liveness probes page): "Many applications running for long periods of time eventually transition to broken states, and cannot recover except by being restarted. Kubernetes provides liveness probes to detect and remedy such situations." probe kinds: command (exec), HTTP request, TCP socket, gRPC.

headline: Probe timing is explicit and periodic.

quoteChecks.quote: `periodSeconds` … the kubelet should perform a liveness probe every 5 seconds

frags.frag: the kubelet should perform a liveness probe every 5 seconds

_hay: quote (S119, probe fields): "The periodSeconds field specifies that the kubelet should perform a liveness probe every 5 seconds. The initialDelaySeconds field tells the kubelet that it should wait 5 seconds before performing the first probe." kubelet-driven: the platform polls the worker; failure → container restart (pod-level reclaim), not job reclaim.

headline: The lane's liveness signal is pull-based, not worker-pushed.
_hay: lane mapping (origin tree read-only, pin 31c465f1): fleet-dispatcher reconcile treats a `launching` claim older than LAUNCHING_GRACE_MS as reclaimable — the lease side. Worker liveness analog: repend fires only on `registered_mission_missing` with a nonzero launcher exit — a pull-based "is the worker still there" signal rather than a worker-pushed heartbeat; MAX_LAUNCH_MISSES bounds false positives.

headline: [INFERENCE] Push-vs-pull is the entry's real axis.
_hay: lane mapping (origin tree read-only, pin 31c465f1): fleet-dispatcher.mjs LAUNCHING_GRACE_MS = 120000 (120 s): a `launching` claim that survives the grace window is reclaimed by reconcile — the pull-based dead-worker slot paired with repend's MAX_LAUNCH_MISSES bound; the dispatcher inspects, the worker never pings.

headline: RabbitMQ heartbeats are transport keepalive, not worker liveness.
